transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you. Well, I came in because I just... I seem to worry about absolutely everything lately. Clients, the housing market, my family, money... even whether moving to the condo was the right decision. Which, you know, downsizing is supposed to make things easier at my age, right? My friend Brenda moved into a condo over in Westlake last year and she just loves it. They have a lovely little pool and a clubhouse where they do water aerobics on Tuesdays. I actually thought about joining a water aerobics class myself, but then I'd have to buy a new swimsuit, and the ones at the department stores are just so poorly made these days. You wash them once and the elastic is completely shot, it's just a waste of money... 

Anyway, I'm sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, the worrying. It just... it all feels so out of proportion to what is actually happening in my life right now. I just can't seem to turn it off.
Have you been avoiding any activities or places because of your worries?

No, I wouldn't say I'm avoiding anything, really. I still go to work, show houses, run my errands... though running errands is getting so frustrating lately with the traffic. They started that construction on 4th Street, and it is just a nightmare. I swear, they've been working on that same stretch of road since last summer. My sister, she lives out in the suburbs, and she keeps telling me I should just order my groceries online to save time. Have you ever tried that? The delivery services? She says it's wonderful, but I just don't trust someone else to pick out my produce. I mean, how do they know if an avocado is perfectly ripe? You have to squeeze it just right. Last time I sent my nephew to the store for me, he brought back bananas that were practically completely brown... 

But, um, no, to answer your question, I'm not staying home or avoiding places. I'm just worrying the whole time I'm out.
Have you noticed any changes in your body when you're worrying, like feeling tense or having trouble sleeping?

Well, yes, actually. I do get this terrible tightness. By the end of the day, my neck and shoulders feel so tight, like I've been bracing myself for something that never happens. And I catch myself clenching my jaw a lot, especially when I'm driving between listings or just sitting at my desk. Which reminds me, my desk chair is just awful. I bought it at one of those big office supply stores, you know, the ones that always smell like printer ink and old carpet? The salesman told me it had "ergonomic lumbar support," but honestly, I think it just pokes me right in the spine. I should have kept my old chair, the leather one, but it got a little tear in the armrest when the movers were bringing it into the condo. They were so careless! One of them actually dropped a box of my good china, the set my mother gave me for my wedding. Thank goodness none of the plates broke, just a little chip on one of the teacups, but still... you pay good money for professionals and they just rush through everything. 

But, um, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the tension. Yes, my neck and shoulders get very tight, and I definitely clench my jaw. As for sleeping, it's just... well, my mind keeps racing.
Do you find yourself having repetitive thoughts that you can't get out of your head?

Well, yes, I suppose I do. It's like... even when I tell myself, "Parin, this is not urgent," I just can't stop. One concern just leads right into another. Like yesterday, I was worrying about an inspection on a property over on Elm Street, and then I started thinking about how the gutters on my own condo probably need cleaning, which made me think about the HOA fees going up next year. Did I tell you they're raising them by fifteen percent? Fifteen percent! And for what? They say it's for landscaping, but they just hired a new company last month and all they do is blow the leaves around with those terribly loud gas leaf blowers. It's such a racket, especially on Thursday mornings when I'm trying to enjoy my coffee on the patio. I bought this lovely new patio set, wrought iron with these beautiful teal cushions, from a catalog. It took six weeks to arrive, and when it finally did, one of the chairs was missing a little rubber foot, so it wobbled. I had to call customer service three times just to get them to send a replacement part... 

But anyway, before I know it, I've spent half an hour just replaying all these small details in my head that I really meant to just let go of. It's exhausting.
Do you ever feel like you have to perform specific rituals or behaviors to reduce your anxiety?

Rituals? No, I wouldn't say that. I don't have to, you know, flip the light switch a certain number of times or wash my hands over and over. I mean, I do like things a certain way when I'm staging a house, of course. You have to make sure the throw pillows are perfectly fluffed. Have you noticed how hard it is to find good throw pillows lately? The ones at the department stores are all so flat now. They use that cheap polyester fill instead of real down. I bought a beautiful set of down-filled cushions for a listing on Maple Drive—oh, it was a gorgeous mid-century modern, sold over asking in two days—but anyway, I left the pillows there by mistake after the open house. The new buyers just kept them! Can you believe that? I called their agent, and he said they thought it was part of the staging that came with the house. People can be so presumptuous. It's like that time I left my favorite umbrella at the hair salon, and when I went back the very next day, the receptionist claimed she hadn't seen it. But it was a very distinctive floral print, you couldn't just miss it... 

But, um... no. I don't do any specific behaviors or rituals to stop the worrying. I just kind of sit there and worry.
Do you find that you're doing things to avoid triggering your worries?

Avoid things? Well, no, not exactly. I mean, I still go to work, I still do my open houses and meet with clients. I don't hide away or anything. I suppose I try to avoid things that I know are going to be a disaster, like driving on Interstate 95 during rush hour. It's just a parking lot out there, and the other drivers are so aggressive. Last week, this enormous pickup truck—one of those lifted ones with the oversized tires, you know?—he just cut right in front of me without even a turn signal. I had to slam on my brakes so hard my purse flew off the passenger seat, and all my lipsticks spilled out. I had just bought this lovely new shade of coral, too. It rolled right under the seat, and I couldn't reach it for three days until I took the car to the wash. 

And speaking of the car wash, they raised their prices again! It used to be twelve dollars for the basic wash, and now it's eighteen. Eighteen dollars just to run it through those giant blue spinning brushes that I'm half convinced leave tiny scratches on the clear coat anyway. My neighbor, Richard, he washes his own car in his driveway every Saturday morning. He uses this special chamois cloth he ordered from Germany. He's very particular about it. He even offered to wash mine once, but I felt terrible imposing on him, especially since his wife just had knee surgery... 

But, um, avoiding things to stop the worry? No, I don't think I do that. The worry just sort of comes with me wherever I go, even if I'm just sitting at home.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind even when you try to think about something else?

Well, I think we just talked about that, didn't we? The repeating thoughts? I mean, yes, they do repeat. Like I was saying about the gutters and the HOA fees. It's just a constant loop. And speaking of loops, I was trying to knit a scarf the other day—a lovely infinity scarf, you know, the ones that just loop around your neck? I found this beautiful merino wool yarn at a little boutique downtown. It's hand-dyed, a sort of sunset ombre, just gorgeous. But the lady who runs the shop, she's always so chatty. I went in just for one skein, and she kept me there for forty-five minutes talking about her daughter's wedding in Tuscany. Which sounds lovely, of course, but who can afford a destination wedding these days? The flights alone! I flew to Chicago last month for a real estate conference, and the airlines are just charging for every little thing now. You want a carry-on? That's extra. You want to pick your seat? Extra. I ended up in a middle seat between two men who both wanted the armrests. 

But anyway... yes, the thoughts just keep repeating, even when I try to focus on something else, like my knitting or a client's paperwork. It's very distracting.
Are there any areas of your life where you don't tend to worry?

Areas where I don't worry? Hmm... I don't think so. I really can't think of any part of my life where I'm not worrying about something. It just seems to touch everything, you know? Like, even when I'm gardening, which is supposed to be relaxing, I'm worrying about the aphids on my roses. I bought this organic neem oil spray because I don't want to use harsh chemicals, especially with the neighbor's cat always wandering into my yard. He's a beautiful orange tabby, named Marmalade. Such a sweet boy, but he loves to dig in my freshly mulched flower beds. I tried putting down cayenne pepper to keep him away—I read that on a gardening blog—but it just washed away in the rain we had on Tuesday. 

Did you see how hard it rained? The storm drains on my street backed up completely. The city really needs to come out and clear the leaves out of the grates. I called public works about it three times last fall, and you just sit on hold listening to that awful elevator music. It’s that same looping jazz track that the dentist’s office plays. I had to get a crown replaced last month because I cracked it on a popcorn kernel at the movies. Twelve dollars for a small popcorn, and it cost me a thousand-dollar dental bill! The movies just aren't worth it anymore. 

But, um, what were you asking? Oh, right, parts of my life without worry. No, I really don't think there are any. It’s just always there.
Do you have thoughts that are intrusive or unwanted, and that you try to suppress or ignore?

Intrusive thoughts? You mean like... things that just pop into my head that I don't want there? No, not really. I mean, my worries are always there, like I said, but they're about real things, you know? Not like... weird or crazy thoughts that I have to push away. 

Although, speaking of pushing things away, I had to completely reorganize my pantry this weekend because I found pantry moths. Can you believe it? I think they came in a bag of organic flour I bought at that new health food store on Elm Street. The store is lovely, very clean, but they have all those bulk bins where anyone can just scoop things out. I usually try to buy everything pre-packaged, but I was making a special sourdough starter. My sister-in-law, Brenda, she started making sourdough during the pandemic and never stopped. She brings a loaf to every family gathering. Honestly, it's a bit dense for my taste, and last Thanksgiving it was practically burnt on the bottom, but nobody says anything because she's so proud of it. 

Anyway, I had to throw out all my grains and pastas. It broke my heart to toss three boxes of imported linguine. I had to scrub every shelf with white vinegar. Vinegar is supposed to be a natural deterrent, you know. I use it for cleaning my windows, too, mixed with a little water and a drop of dish soap. It leaves them completely streak-free, unlike those blue commercial sprays that just smear the dirt around. I learned that trick from my grandmother... 

But, no, I don't get those kinds of thoughts. Just the regular worrying about everything.
Do you feel like your worrying is interfering with your ability to work or enjoy time with friends and family?

Well, yes, I suppose it is. Especially at work. Even straightforward listing negotiations and contract reviews are taking me much longer than they used to. I had this one listing last week, a beautiful mid-century modern split-level over on Oak Creek Drive. The sellers are retiring to Florida. Sarasota, I think. Sarasota has that lovely Ringling Museum with the miniature circus. I took my niece there when she was ten. She's twenty-four now and working in digital marketing, whatever that means. She tries to explain it to me, but it just sounds like she looks at her phone all day. 

But anyway, the contract for that house was so simple, just standard boilerplate, but I kept reading it over and over. I’ve actually had to delay returning client calls because I just don’t feel confident I’ve checked everything carefully enough. And speaking of calls, the amount of spam calls I get on my cell phone lately is just outrageous. They always tell me my car warranty is expiring. I drive a 2021 Lexus, I know exactly when my warranty expires! I had to download one of those call-blocking apps, but it blocked my sister by mistake. She was furious because she was trying to reach me to organize our cousin's baby shower. We're doing a Peter Rabbit theme. So classic, don't you think? Much better than those gender reveal parties with the colored smoke that always seem to start forest fires. People just don't think about the environmental impact of those things. 

But, um... what was I saying? Oh, right, work. Yes, it’s definitely interfering because I just can't seem to get through my paperwork without second-guessing myself.
Is there even a single activity or part of your daily routine where you find yourself completely worry-free?

Worry-free? No, not at all. Honestly, that's exactly why I came in to see you. I just seem to worry about absolutely everything now—my clients, the housing market, my family, money, even whether moving to the condo was the right decision. And I know it feels completely out of proportion to what is actually happening, but I just can't stop it. 

Like with the condo... I thought downsizing would mean less stress, but the homeowner's association is just terribly strict. They have rules about everything. You can't even have a welcome mat that isn't pre-approved by the board! I had bought this lovely coir mat with little bluebirds on it from a craft fair up in Vermont. My friend Susan and I go every October for the foliage. The leaves were a bit dull this year, though. Someone said it was because we didn't get enough rain in August. We stayed at this quaint little bed and breakfast, but the mattress was like sleeping on a slab of granite. My back ached for a week after we got home. I tried taking Epsom salt baths—the Dr. Teal's lavender one, which usually helps so much. I always buy it in bulk at Costco. Have you seen how crowded Costco gets on a Saturday? You can barely get your cart down the aisle, especially around the sample stations. People just abandon their carts right in the middle of the walkway for a tiny piece of a frozen taquito... 

But, um, what were you asking me? Oh, right, an activity where I don't worry. No. No, there really isn't one. It just follows me everywhere.
Do you often feel restless or on edge?

Restless? I suppose so, yes. I just feel like I can't ever truly settle down. It's like this constant buzzing feeling under my skin, you know? Just always wound up. 

It actually reminds me of my old rescue dog, Buster. He was a terrier mix, the sweetest thing, but he had this terrible anxiety during thunderstorms. He would pace the hallways for hours, just back and forth, clicking his little nails on the hardwood floors. Click, click, click. We tried everything for him. Those little thunder shirts? Completely useless. I ended up having to buy him these special calming treats with chamomile in them. I got them from this little boutique pet store downtown. The owner there, Margaret, she used to be a real estate agent too, actually. Small world, isn't it? She left the business back in 2008 when the market crashed. Said she couldn't handle the stress of short sales anymore. I can't blame her, really. Short sales are a nightmare of paperwork. You have to deal with the banks, and they move at a glacial pace. I had one last year that took nine months to close! Nine months! The buyers almost walked away three times. They ended up having a baby before they even got the keys to the house. A little boy, I think. Or maybe it was a girl? They sent me a birth announcement, but the picture was so blurry it was hard to tell. People really rely too much on their phone cameras these days. My niece tried to tell me the new iPhone takes better pictures than a professional camera, but I just don't believe it. You need a proper lens for good portraits. 

But anyway, yes, restless. That's exactly how I feel. Just like poor Buster pacing the floors.
Is your worry usually about one main thing or many different things at the same time?

Well, that's the thing, it's really about everything all at once. I think I mentioned it a minute ago, actually, but it's like my brain just jumps from one disaster to the next. I worry about my clients, of course, and the housing market—which is just so unpredictable right now with the interest rates. And then I start worrying about my family, and my savings, and even if selling the house and moving into that condo was a huge mistake. 

Speaking of the condo, I was just looking at the utility bill yesterday, and the electricity is somehow higher than it was in my four-bedroom house! How does that even make sense? I called the power company, and you know how it is when you try to call customer service these days. You just get stuck in that endless automated loop. "Press 1 for billing, press 2 for service..." And then the voice recognition never understands what you're saying. I was shouting "Representative! Representative!" into the phone for ten minutes. My neighbor, Mrs. Gable, must have thought I was losing my mind. She's a sweet older lady, but she has this habit of leaving her trash bags out in the hallway instead of walking them down to the chute. The HOA sent out a memo about it, but she just ignores it. It really attracts those little fruit flies, especially in the summer. I bought one of those little apple-shaped traps you fill with vinegar, but they smell terrible. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the worrying. Yes, it's just so many different things at the same time. And I know it's completely out of proportion to what's actually going on, but I just can't seem to turn it off.
Have you ever experienced a sudden, intense fear or discomfort that reaches a peak within minutes and includes symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or shortness of breath?

Sudden intense fear? Like a panic attack, you mean? No, I don't think I've ever had anything quite like that. My heart doesn't race like I'm having a heart attack or anything. It's more just this steady, exhausting hum of worry all day long. 

Though speaking of racing hearts, my sister Elaine called me last week in an absolute state. She thought she was having a heart attack right in the middle of the grocery store. Turned out it was just really bad indigestion from this spicy Thai food she had for lunch. I told her, "Elaine, you're 63, you can't eat green curry like you're in your twenties anymore." She never listens to me. She's always been stubborn, even when we were kids. We used to share a bedroom in this old Victorian house my parents owned, and she insisted on painting her half of the room this atrocious neon pink color. It was the 70s, you know, so everyone had questionable taste, but this pink was just blinding. I had to put up a curtain down the middle of the room just so I could sleep at night. I found that curtain years later in the attic when we were clearing out the house after my dad passed. It smelled entirely of mothballs. Do they even sell mothballs anymore? I feel like you never see them in stores. Cedar blocks are so much better anyway. I put cedar blocks in all my closets at the condo to protect my winter coats. I have this gorgeous wool peacoat I bought in New York City five years ago, and I would just die if moths got to it. 

But no, I've never had a sudden attack like you're describing. Just the constant, everyday worrying.
Has your worrying affected your relationships with family or friends?

My relationships? Well, I suppose my friends have noticed I'm a bit more... distracted lately. I haven't been going to our Thursday night book club as much. But honestly, it's mostly affecting my work. I'm a real estate broker, you know, and lately, even the most straightforward listing negotiations and contract reviews are taking me just... so much longer than they used to. I keep second-guessing myself. I've even had to delay returning client calls because I just don't feel confident I've checked everything carefully enough. 

It's so frustrating because I used to be so sharp with contracts. Back when I started in the 90s, we didn't have all these digital signatures and online portals. You actually sat down with people at a kitchen table with a pen. I remember this one couple, the Hendersons, they bought this lovely little split-level ranch. They brought over a freshly baked cherry pie for the signing. You don't see that anymore, do you? People baking for their real estate agents. Now everyone is just so rushed, rushing to the next thing, eating those awful protein bars in their cars. I tried one of those bars once, my niece left it in my car—the one with the iPhone, you know. It tasted exactly like cardboard and artificial sweetener. I don't understand how people consider that a meal. Food should be enjoyed, like a good roast chicken or a nice beef stew. I make a wonderful beef stew, actually. The secret is a splash of red wine and letting it simmer for at least four hours. The smell just fills the whole condo, which is nice because it covers up the smell of Mrs. Gable's fruit fly vinegar traps in the hallway. 

But anyway, yes, the worrying... it's definitely making work much harder than it needs to be. I just can't seem to trust myself to get the paperwork right the first time anymore.
Is your worrying generally about everyday things and situations, or is it more focused on a specific area of your life, such as work or finances?

Well, like I think I mentioned when we first started talking, it's really just... everything. It's not just work or finances, though those are definitely on the list. I seem to worry about everything now—my clients, the real estate market, my family, money... even whether selling the house and moving to that condo was the right decision. And I know it feels completely out of proportion to what is actually happening, but I just can't seem to stop. 

Take the condo, for instance. I was looking at the balcony yesterday, and I bought these beautiful terracotta planters for it to try and make it feel more like home. They were supposedly imported from Italy, from this lovely little nursery down on 4th Street. Have you been there? The owner, Marcus, he has the most gorgeous golden retriever that just sleeps right by the cash register. I always want to pet him, but I'm usually in my nice work clothes, and you know how dog hair just clings to everything. Especially black slacks. I use those sticky lint rollers, but they never get quite all of it. I buy them in bulk at Costco now. Costco is just a madhouse on the weekends, though. People pushing those giant carts around like they're in a bumper car arena. I saw a woman nearly take out an entire display of extra virgin olive oil last time I was there. 

But... what was I saying? Oh, right. Yes, everyday things, specific things, all of it. It's just a constant worry about absolutely everything, and it's definitely out of proportion to reality.
Have you ever experienced a sudden feeling of intense fear or anxiety that lasted for a short period of time?

Well, wait, didn't you just ask me that? About the sudden panic and the heart racing? I think I already mentioned, no, I haven't had anything sudden like that. It's really just the constant hum of worrying all the time. 

Though... you know, speaking of sudden things, the fire alarm in my condo building went off at 3 AM the other night. Scared the living daylights out of me. It was that awful, piercing screech that practically vibrates in your teeth. I grabbed my robe—it's this lovely plush navy blue one my niece got me for Christmas, the one who left the protein bar in my car—and I hurried out into the hallway. And there was Mrs. Gable, standing there in her curlers, holding a parakeet cage. I didn't even know she had a bird! They're supposedly against the HOA rules. The HOA is so strict about pets. They sent out a memo last month saying even visiting dogs aren't allowed in the lobby. Can you believe that? I mean, what if my sister Elaine wanted to visit and bring her schnauzer? Not that she would, she hates driving in the city. She says the traffic makes her nervous. 

But anyway, to answer your question again, no. No sudden attacks of fear. Just the everyday, all-day worry.
Has your worrying significantly impacted your daily life or relationships in a way that you feel is unbearable or causing substantial problems?

Well, I think I touched on this a bit earlier, didn't I? It's really my work that's taking the hit. Like I said, those straightforward listing negotiations and contract reviews... they're just taking me so much longer now. I used to breeze through them. Now I'm delaying returning client calls because I just don't feel confident I've checked everything carefully enough. 

It's embarrassing, really. Just last week, I had a client, Mr. Thompson—lovely man, looking for a little pied-à-terre downtown. He’s a retired dentist. Did you know dentists have some of the highest rates of back problems? It makes sense, I suppose, hunched over people's mouths all day. My own dentist, Dr. Evans, he has this special ergonomic chair he sits in. It looks like something out of a spaceship. He was telling me about it while he was doing my cleaning last month. I hate the scraping sound they make, don't you? It sets my teeth on edge, literally. But he's very gentle. He always asks about my niece. 

Anyway, I kept Mr. Thompson waiting for two days on a simple disclosure form because I just kept reading it over and over. So, yes, it's definitely causing problems. It's just so frustrating to feel like I can't trust my own eyes anymore.
Is there a particular area in your life where you feel your worrying is most prominent or is it spread out across multiple areas?

Well, I feel like I'm repeating myself a bit, but it really is spread out across everything. Like I was saying before, it's work, it's money, it's my family, the condo... it's just a constant hum about all of it. There isn't really one single thing that stands out because it all just sort of blends together into one big worry. 

Speaking of blending together, I was trying to make a smoothie this morning to take my vitamins. I read somewhere that taking vitamins on an empty stomach isn't good for absorption. Or maybe it was just that it causes nausea? I can't remember. Anyway, I put some spinach and frozen blueberries in the blender—the blueberries were on sale at Whole Foods. I love Whole Foods, but their parking lot is a nightmare. The spaces are so narrow. I always worry someone is going to ding my car door. It's a lease, you see, and they charge you an arm and a leg for any little scratch when you turn it in. My last car, a Honda CR-V, had this tiny little scuff on the bumper from a shopping cart, and they made such a fuss about it. 

But yes, to answer your question, it's not just one area. It's really everything, all the time.
